lines: Welcome to workstation.
This machine is yours to explore. Nothing you do here can hurt
your real computer: every file, user and process is simulated.
A few rules of the road:
* Commands are case-sensitive. LS is not ls.
* Tab completes names. Arrow Up recalls what you typed.
* Stuck? Type :hint.  Curious? Type help, or man <command>.
The first codeword is: LANTERN
P.S. Not everything in this directory shows up when you list it.
You found me.
Files whose names start with a dot are hidden from a plain `ls`.
They are usually configuration: .bashrc, .profile, .ssh/ ...
The second codeword is: ORBIT
# ~/.bashrc: executed by bash for interactive shells.
export EDITOR=nano
alias ll='ls -l'
